newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes slightly firmer, little business.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes slightly firmer, little business.

text.p: Gold prices drifted slightly higher in quiet trade on Monday reflecting New York being closed for the President's Day holiday.
Gold was fixed at $344.10 per ounce after $343.60 in the morning and $342.40 on Friday afternoon.
"Business will more or less finish after the afternoon fixing given there is no trade going on in New York," one dealer said.
Gold has managed a sizeable bounce from its 3-3/4 year low of $336.90 posted last Wednesday.
Even so, dealers were wary of saying gold had shaken off the bear trend which had pressured prices since the beginning of the year.

"While the market is making a technical correction and further consolidation is a reasonable expectation today, there are few positive fundamentals around for the medium term," brokers GNI said in a report.
Palladium came off a low bid of $131.25 early today to $133.00/$134.00 just a dollar off Friday's close.
It reached its highest fixing since March 27 last year at $141.25 on Thursday on fund and trade buying spurred by the delayed Russia-Japan export contract negotiations for 1997.

However the impetus behind palladium has slowed since Russia's upper house passed the country's budget and a Russian official said on Friday export talks could start in March with deliveries beginning the following month.
Heavy selling in Tokyo early on Monday pushed palladium to a morning fix of $130.75, down $5.75 from Friday afternoon.
"The white metals seem to be leading the way but I am not expecting any fireworks today, just some position squaring," a dealer said.
Platinum followed its sister metal lower to $363.00/$364.00, $2.50 off Friday's close.
Silver's bid to break higher on Friday hit resistance over $5.25 but was still four cents above the Friday close at $5.20/$5.22.
Friday's run up was driven by positioning ahead of the Comex option expiry which centred on $5.25 March calls.
"It could drift lower with the expiry out of the way but on the charts silver still looks pretty good," one dealer said.
